finding.claim: Authorization bypass in the ban endpoint. require_admin() denies access by calling abort(403), which raises an HTTPException. The ban() handler wraps that call in `except Exception`, so the denial is caught and only logged. Execution then continues to do_ban(uid), so any authenticated non-admin user can ban arbitrary users. The unban route does not wrap the call and is correctly protected.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, a privileged operation that bans a user

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban accepts POST; uid is attacker-controlled
require_admin(g.user) is called inside a try block
A non-admin triggers abort(403), which raises werkzeug HTTPException (a subclass of Exception)
The handler only logs a warning and does not return or re-raise. It also logs the user-controlled name field.
do_ban(uid) executes regardless of the admin check result

finding.guards_checked: require_admin is the only guard. Its effect is negated by the broad except. No other decorator, before_request hook or middleware exists in the file. The unban route at line 26 calls require_admin without a try/except, so it is not affected.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() at admin.py:9-11 aborts with 403, but ban() wraps it in `except Exception` (admin.py:18) and doesn't return or re-raise. There is no before_request hook or decorator in the file.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:16-20, abort(403) (raised at line 11, triggered by the check at line 10) is swallowed by `except Exception`, which only logs, so do_ban(uid) at line 20 runs for any authenticated non-admin. The unban route at line 26 is unwrapped and stays protected.

verdict_facts.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 on failure, but ban() wraps it in try/except Exception (admin.py:16-19), so the denial is swallowed. No decorator, before_request hook or other check exists.
